fl_furrow_end.name: The Long Furrow — the Foot
fl_furrow_end.desc: The Bone Road ends where the ground was cut open once and never properly closed: a single grave the length of a field, banked with forty years of settling earth. It does not look like two hundred people. It looks like a wound that never scarred over right.
fl_furrow_end.brief: The furrow's foot, long and unhealed.
onEnterOnce: This is the whole cost of the Winter of Lying Down, laid end to end because nobody was left standing to dig it any other way. Whatever rests it, bargains with it, or burns it, that choice is yours now.
Vell: "Two hundred names, and not one record anywhere that lists them properly. History prefers its dead in smaller, tidier numbers. This is what it looks like when it can't have that."

fl_furrow_walk.name: The Long Furrow — the Walking
fl_furrow_walk.desc: Walking its length takes longer than it should for a single grave. Markers thin out and thicken again in patches, whole stretches of ground with nothing driven into them at all — the ones nobody was left alive to mark.
fl_furrow_walk.brief: The long walk down the grave's length.

variants.desc: Walking its length takes longer than it should. Near the southern end, the ground is newer than the rest by decades — grass only just taking hold. Someone's father, most likely, waiting on a name.
variants.brief: The long walk. One newer stretch, at the south end.

fl_furrow_heart.name: The Long Furrow — the Cairn
fl_furrow_heart.desc: A single cairn stands at the furrow's far end, stones added by hand over forty years by whoever passed and couldn't leave it entirely unmarked. It is the only thing here that looks tended. It is not enough, and everyone who built it knew that.
fl_furrow_heart.brief: The cairn, the only tended thing here.
onEnterOnce: Osk: "A fever, the record says. I have stood at the edge of this and I do not believe the record ever once. Someone wrote that word down to make the silence afterward easier to keep."
Tamsin: "Forty years of somebody stacking one stone at a time because nobody would send more hands. That's not neglect. That's a whole hold being told to manage on its own."

actions.label: speak the names, rite, and verse
fx: You speak every name the roll, the markers, and Ede gave up, then the Church's rite, then Frey's rest-verse to close it — three unfinished duties done at once, forty years late. The cairn needs no other stone after this.
One name among the two hundred is only weeks old. You say it in its proper turn, no different from the rest.

actions.label: swear the land stays theirs (will)
fx: You swear it plain over the cairn: this ground stays the Fallows' own, no stakes, no muster, for as long as the promise holds. Something in the air over the furrow settles, and does not test you twice.
The words come out uncertain, and whatever was listening does not settle for uncertain. It can be tried again, once you're sure you mean every part of it.

actions.label: raise stones the whole length (might)
fx: You spend a day setting a stone over every unmarked stretch, until the whole length is tended, not only the cairn. It isn't a rite. It's care, plainly given, and the furrow takes it as close enough.
The stones you set are heavier than the ground wants to hold, and half of them settle crooked before nightfall. It can be tried again, with steadier hands or better luck.

actions.label: burn it with cinder-oil (1hp on fail)
fx: The oil takes fast along the cut, and the furrow burns a night and a day. By morning there is nothing left to rest, bargain, or grieve over — only cleared black ground, and a cairn standing pointlessly over it.
The oil catches wrong in the damp ground and flares back before it spreads. You're driven off a step, singed, the furrow untouched.

stages.text: Names, rite, and verse are all yours. Speak them together at the cairn to rest the furrow whole.
You carry Ironbound cinder-oil. Burn the furrow at the cairn, if that's the ending you'll answer for.
Rest it (names, rite, verse), bargain it (a vow or raised stones), or burn it (Ironbound oil) — all at the cairn.
The Bone Road south of the crossroads leads to the headland, and past it, the furrow itself.
Wickstead's whole dead lie in one long, unrested furrow, south past the fallow fields.
Two of three found. The last waits in Ede's memory, the parish roll, or the headland's markers.
One source found. Two remain: Ede's memory, the parish roll, the headland's markers.
The rite needs the names whole: some from Ede's memory, more from the parish roll, the rest from the headland's markers.

epilogue.text: The Long Furrow rests at last, forty years and three name-sources late. Wickstead sleeps through the night now.
The furrow took a promise instead of a rite: the Fallows stay the hold's own, no stakes, no muster — while the promise holds.
Ironbound oil cleared the Long Furrow in a night. There is nothing left there now to rest, bargain with, or grieve over.
The Long Furrow still lies open south of Wickstead, unrested, unbargained, unburned, exactly as the winter left it.
The Fallows reverted to the Crown. Surveyor Pell's stakes stand in every field the escheat ever claimed.
The Free Companies kept the Fallows' muster barn for good. Recruiter Dace never did run short of the desperate.
The Fallows went to the returners. Sister Merrow still rings the chapel bell early on the anniversary.
The Fallows lie fallow by the old covenant. Frey finally wrote to Barrowmere and signed the letter Keeper.
Wickstead's bargain with its own dead did not hold. Nobody there talks about what that cost, exactly.
The bargain held a while longer on borrowed coin. Someone will have to keep paying it, eventually.
Dain's father went unnamed in the end, same as the day he died. The boy stopped asking, but not waiting.
Dain's father got a name spoken over him after all, the same as the two hundred who lay down before him.
Dain still watches the drilling through the gap in the barn wall. His father's name went unspoken, one way or another.
Old Ede keeps her wicker house, watched now, warm in a dead man's cloak she finally let herself wear.
